Tocar a escala maior com 3 notas em cada: Play the major scale with 3 notes on each string
Bem-vindo ao mês 9. O braço inteiro vai: Welcome to month 9. The whole neck is about to connect: three scale systems and the seven modes.
No **3NPS** (*three notes per string*),: In **3NPS** (*three notes per string*), every string has exactly **3 notes**. Picking becomes regular (↓↑↓ ↑↓↑…), and the scale covers **two and a half octaves** in a single region.
Dó maior em 3NPS a partir da casa 8 (cor: C major in 3NPS from fret 8 (string 6). Notice the 5-fret stretch on some strings.
3NPS requires stretching your hand (up to 5 frets). Warm up first and don't force it: use finger 4 on the big stretches, without twisting your wrist.
Com 3 notas por corda, a palhetada alter: With 3 notes per string, strict alternate picking makes each string start in the opposite direction from the last. Good for the right hand.
Ver onde um termina e o outro começa: See where one ends and the next begins
Subir o braço pela escala: Climb the neck through the scale
Cada padrão começa na **próxima nota da: Each pattern starts on the **next scale note** on string 6. In C: fret 8 (C), 10 (D), 12 (E), and then back down: fret 1 (F), 3 (G), 5 (A), 7 (B).
Conhecer os 7 padrões de Dó maior: Learn the 7 patterns of C major
São **7 padrões** porque a escala tem 7: There are **7 patterns** because the scale has 7 notes. Each one starts on a different degree. It's a first contact with modes, but careful: a **pattern** isn't a **mode**. The mode depends on the harmony, not on the fret where you start.
A escala em uma corda só: The scale on a single string
Tocar numa corda só obriga a **ver as di: Playing on one string forces you to **see the distances**: whole step = 2 frets, half step = 1. It's the clearest way to see a scale's shape, and it's how the sitar, the mandolin and many slide guitarists think.
Use slides para trocar de região: dedo 1: Use slides to change regions: finger 1 slides to the next note every two or three notes.
Tocar a mesma escala de três jeitos: Play the same scale three ways
Escolher o sistema conforme a música: Choose the system for the music
**CAGED** (mês 4): ancorado nos acordes,: **CAGED** (month 4): anchored to chords, great for seeing the root, 3rd and 5th.
**3NPS:** palhetada regular, ótimo para: **3NPS:** regular picking, great for speed and long phrases.
**Linear:** liberdade horizontal, slides: **Linear:** horizontal freedom, slides, a vocal sound.
Nenhum é *o certo*. A meta é que os três: None of them is *the right one*. The goal is for all three to merge into a single map in your head.
O desafio pede **escalas ligadas em toda: The challenge asks for **connected scales in every position at 100 BPM** (eighth notes). Today you measure where you are.
Escada de andamento: 80 → 85 → 90 → 95 →: Tempo ladder: 80 → 85 → 90 → 95 → 100. Only go up when you play it **clean twice**.

Achar 9, 11 e 13 sobre o acorde: Find the 9, 11 and 13 over a chord
Sobre um acorde, as notas da escala que: Over a chord, the scale notes that **aren't** 1, 3, 5 or 7 are the **tensions**: the 2nd becomes the **9**, the 4th the **11**, the 6th the **13** (counted in the upper octave).
**Regra prática:** uma nota **um tom aci: **Rule of thumb:** a note **a whole step above** a chord tone is an **available tension**: it sounds good held. E.g.: over Cmaj7, **D** (9) is a whole step above C.
D (9) soa doce; A (13) soa aberto; F# (#: D (9) sounds sweet; A (13) sounds open; F# (#11) sounds *Lydian*, modern.
Usar a 4ª no maior só de passagem: Use the 4th in major only in passing
Meio tom acima do acorde: A half step above the chord
Uma nota **meio tom acima** de uma nota: A note **a half step above** a chord tone tends to be an **avoid note**: held, it clashes. Use it **in passing**, resolving.
**Jônio (Cmaj7):** a 4ª (**F**) fica mei: **Ionian (Cmaj7):** the 4th (**F**) is a half step above E.
**Mixolídio (G7):** a 4ª (**C**) fica me: **Mixolydian (G7):** the 4th (**C**) is a half step above B.
**Eólio (Am7):** a b6 (**F**) fica meio: **Aeolian (Am7):** the b6 (**F**) is a half step above E.
**Dórico como iim7 (Dm7):** a 6ª (**B**): **Dorian as iim7 (Dm7):** the 6th (**B**) is usually avoided in a tonal context.
F segurado × F de passagem sobre Cmaj7: Held F × passing F over Cmaj7
O F segurado soa como *erro*. O F que de: The held F sounds like a *mistake*. The F that moves down to E sounds like *melody*. Same note, different function.

O jeito certo de aprender modos: The right way to learn modes
Um **modo** é uma escala com uma **cor p: A **mode** is a scale with **its own color**, heard over **a fixed root**. That's why this month you play every mode **over a C drone**: C Ionian, C Dorian, C Phrygian… That way each mode really sounds different.
Tocar as notas de Dó maior começando no: Playing C major's notes starting on D **is not** *D Dorian* if the music is in C. Your ear keeps hearing C. The mode depends on the harmony underneath.
Cada modo tem uma **nota característica*: Each mode has a **characteristic note**: the one that sets it apart from the closest major or minor. That's the note you'll highlight in a modal solo.
Tocar Dó jônio e Dó lídio: Play C Ionian and C Lydian
Dó jônio, casas 7 a 10. A escala maior d: C Ionian, frets 7 to 10. The good old major scale.
O **lídio** é a escala maior com a **4ª: **Lydian** is the major scale with an **augmented 4th** (#4): in C, **F#** instead of F. Ionian's avoid note disappears and the sound becomes *floating*, like a space-movie soundtrack.
C Lydian. F# is the characteristic note.
Pouse no F# e segure. Se soar bonito em: Land on F# and hold it. If it sounds beautiful instead of wrong, you're hearing Lydian.
Usar sobre dominante e no baião: Use it over dominants and in baião
O **mixolídio** é a escala maior com a *: **Mixolydian** is the major scale with a **minor 7th** (b7): in C, **Bb**. It's the scale of the **7** (dominant) chord and the sound of classic rock, major-key blues and **baião**.
Dó mixolídio. O Bb é a nota característi: C Mixolydian. Bb is the characteristic note.
Vamp mixolídio típico: **C – Bb** (I – b: A typical Mixolydian vamp: **C – Bb** (I – bVII) or a static **C7**.
Usar sobre m7 em vamp: Use it over an m7 vamp
O **dórico** é a escala menor com a **6ª: **Dorian** is the minor scale with a **major 6th**: in C, **A** instead of Ab. It sounds minor, but *bright*, with groove. It's the sound of funk, modal jazz and a lot of Latin rock.
Dó dórico. O A (6ª maior) é a nota carac: C Dorian. A (the major 6th) is the characteristic note.
Tensão = 1 tom acima de nota do acorde: Tension = a whole step above a chord tone

Tocar Dó eólio e Dó frígio: Play C Aeolian and C Phrygian
**Eólio** (menor natural): b3, b6, b7. E: **Aeolian** (natural minor): b3, b6, b7. In C: **Ab** is the characteristic note compared with Dorian.
**Frígio:** eólio com **b2**. Em Dó: **D: **Phrygian:** Aeolian with a **b2**. In C: **Db**. It sounds Spanish, Middle Eastern, metal.
Dó frígio. O Db (b2) é a nota caracterís: C Phrygian. Db (b2) is the characteristic note.
Saber por que ele é raro como centro: Know why it's rare as a tonal center
O **lócrio** é o frígio com **b5**: em D: **Locrian** is Phrygian with a **b5**: in C, **Gb**. The tonic triad is **diminished** (C Eb Gb): it doesn't sound like rest. That's why it's rarely the center of a whole song. It lives over the **m7(b5)**, like the ii of the minor ii–V.
Dó lócrio. O Gb (b5) é a nota caracterís: C Locrian. Gb (b5) is the characteristic note.
Sobre o Bm7b5 do ii–V menor, a escala de: Over the Bm7b5 of the minor ii–V, the **B Locrian** scale is the notes of A natural minor. You already played this in month 8 without knowing its name.

Ordem de brilho: **lídio → jônio → mixol: Order of brightness: **Lydian → Ionian → Mixolydian → Dorian → Aeolian → Phrygian → Locrian**. From one to the next, **a single note** drops a half step.
Sete modos de Dó (uma oitava cada): Seven modes of C (one octave each)
Não resolver como no tonal: Don't resolve like in tonal music
Na música **tonal**, os acordes caminham: In **tonal** music, chords move toward the tonic (ii–V–I). In **modal** music, the harmony **stays put** on one or two chords (the *vamp*), and the interest is in the **mode's color**.
Vamp dórico clássico: **Dm7 – G7** repet: A classic Dorian vamp: **Dm7 – G7** repeated. It looks like a ii–V, but G7 **doesn't resolve** to C: it goes back to Dm7. Then your ear accepts **D** as the tonic, and the scale is **D Dorian**.
Ré dórico, casas 5 a 8. Característica:: D Dorian, frets 5 to 8. Characteristic: B natural.
**Mixolídio:** **G – F** (I – bVII). Esc: **Mixolydian:** **G – F** (I – bVII). **G Mixolydian** scale. Characteristic: F.
O vamp **E – F** é o som do frígio: o F: The **E – F** vamp is the Phrygian sound: F (b2) falls a half step onto E. With an **E major** chord, the scale becomes **Phrygian dominant** (Phrygian with a major 3rd, G#), which you'll explore in month 10.
Mi frígio na primeira posição: só notas: E Phrygian in first position: natural notes only.
A **cadência andaluza** do flamenco: **A: Flamenco's **Andalusian cadence**: **Am – G – F – E**, ending on E major.
Lídio → jônio → mixolídio → dórico → eól: Lydian → Ionian → Mixolydian → Dorian → Aeolian → Phrygian → Locrian

Se você tocar só a pentatônica sobre Am7: If you only play the pentatonic over Am7–D7, your ear can't tell whether it's Dorian or Aeolian. The **characteristic note** (F#) needs to show up, preferably on a **strong beat** or a **long note**.
Grave e confira: o F# aparece em pelo me: Record and check: does F# show up on at least 3 strong beats?
